issue.title: Inconsistent widths when UTF8 characters are used
{:N?} miscomputes the width of debug-escaped output
issue.body:
```c++
fmt::print("[{:1?}]\n", std::string(""));  // ["]        missing the closing quote
fmt::print("[{:6?}]\n", 'a');              // ['a'     ] padded to 8, not 6
```

The width is computed from the size before escaping, so debug output pads wrong, and for an
empty string the closing quote gets truncated. `std::format` prints `[""]` and `['a'   ]`.

Happy to put up a PR.

issue.title: Characters added after Unicode 13.0 are escaped as unprintable
issue.body:
`fmt::detail::is_printable` was generated by `support/printable.py` in 2021 from Unicode 13.0 data and hasn't been regenerated since. As a result, the 15,942 code points assigned in Unicode 14.0 through 17.0 are treated as unassigned (`Cn`) and get escaped by the debug presentation (`{:?}`) and by range/tuple formatting, which is not what [format.string.escaped] asks for.

This affects, among others:

- common emoji such as 🫠 U+1FAE0 MELTING FACE (Unicode 14.0)
- 9,140 CJK Unified Ideographs, e.g. U+31350 from Extension H (Unicode 15.0), which are used in personal and place names

```c++
#include <fmt/ranges.h>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

int main() {
  fmt::print("{}\n", std::vector<std::string>{"🫠", "\U00031350"});
  fmt::print("{:?}\n", "🫠");
}
```

Output on current `main`:

```
["\U0001fae0", "\U00031350"]
"\U0001fae0"
```

Expected:

```
["🫠", "𱍐"]
"🫠"
```

Note that `test/ranges-test.cc` currently uses U+2A6DE as an example of an unassigned code point, but it has been assigned since Unicode 14.0.

Rerunning `support/printable.py` against the current UnicodeData.txt fixes this.

issue.title: FMT_COMPILE fails to format std::array
fmt fails to properly print time values prior to the POSIX epoch
fmt::formatted_size does not work with fmt::wformat_string
issue.body:
I maintain a library at my work that supports both `char` and `wchar` strings. We use `fmt::formatted_size` to help us mange our memory allocations, but it does not work with `fmt::wformat_string`, requiring me to maintain a fork that adds this support.

The crux of the issue is that `detail::format_string_char_t<S>` does not provide a value when `S` is a `fmt::wformat_string`. Adding an overload of `fmt::formatted_size` that takes a `fmt::wformat_string` specifically resolves the issue. I unfortunately do not currently have legal approval to provide that patch upstream, so I am making this issue to raise the problem and hopefully someone will be able to contribute the necessary fix.

issue.title: Tuple-like type becomes unformattable if `<fmt/ranges.h>` is included
issue.body:
I have a library that provides a type that for convenience can be destructed like so:
```cpp
auto [key, value] = obj;
```
To make the type formattable without having a dependency on fmtlib itself I provide a `format_as` function in the same namespace
```cpp
std::string format_as(FooType const& value) {
   // ...
}
```

This works fine, except if `<fmt/ranges.h>` has been included somewhere, where the following error appears:
```cpp
/opt/compiler-explorer/libs/fmt/12.0.0/include/fmt/ranges.h:172:21: error: no matching function for call to 'fmt::v12::detail::is_tuple_formattable_<lib::FooType, char, true>::check(fmt::v12::detail::tuple_index_sequence<lib::FooType>)'
  172 |       decltype(check(tuple_index_sequence<T>{}))::value;
```
I've tested on 12.2.0 and trunk and got the same issue on both versions.
Full code: https://godbolt.org/z/GPEWoe3Y5

issue.title: inf and nan are left-aligned with a bare width
issue.body:
`inf` and `nan` are left-aligned with a bare width, while finite values are right-aligned:

```cpp
fmt::print("[{:10}]\n", 1.5);   // [       1.5]
fmt::print("[{:10}]\n", inf);   // [inf       ]
```

`std::format` right-aligns both, as does `printf("%10f")`, and the docs give right as the default for numeric types.

In `format.h` the nonfinite path takes the string default rather than the numeric one.

I have a patch for it, +7/-6 with a test, but it changes output for anyone formatting a possibly-nonfinite double with a bare width. Is the current behaviour intended?
